html: Shot Studio — a small film set
A small set. Your point of view.
Stage two performers, find your angles, and cut a little film.
Ready. Rehearse the starter film or arrange your own scene.
Cuts follow the shot list. Characters perform continuously across cuts. Exports are silent, recorded in real time at 960 × 540.

Keep up to four actual recordings with their captured editable films. The take notebook is separate from your current scene. Imported film/video associations and timestamps are supplied, unverified declarations.
No saved takes yet. Finish scene edits and record a committed film.
This recording is only in memory. Retry saving or select it to download its complete backup before leaving. Another recording or import waits for this take to be saved or deliberately discarded.

Recordings are silent WebM, at most 32 MiB each. Playback uses the actual retained bytes; your current stage and raw scene fields stay unchanged. Complete take backups include one recording and its immutable captured film. Hashes verify bytes, not the truth of an imported pairing.
Authored blocking replaces the looping pace with timed marks on the whole film. Name and costume apply to every cue.

Add uses the current global preview position, action and visibility. Each cue restarts the action phase, including a wave. Preview cue uses the film camera at that time, which may be the next shot at a cut. Selecting a cue only changes the editing target.
Performer close-up targets the selected performer’s base position.
Presets change this endpoint and the whole shot’s field of view.
Use current preview is available when this editing shot is on screen. Travel moves the camera in a straight line; it does not avoid performers or scenery.
Unsent edits. The preview and Save project use the committed film. Correct the fields or discard them before switching or recording.

In a compatible headset, look around the courtyard. Aim a controller at the floor and select to place the chosen performer. Squeeze to capture your headset view into the selected editing endpoint; its lens stays unchanged. The other endpoint is preserved and the complete travel path must remain valid. Return to desktop to undo. Camera roll is not captured.
VR placement will edit performer 1’s looping base position.
WebXR support is experimental. Physical headset comfort and controller behavior await device testing.

Copy complete editable scenes, then arrange whole shots. Sources are detached snapshots, not linked edits or spliced recordings. Each clip keeps its original source clock, performers, camera and light.
Reading the complete saved sequence. Nothing is played or rewritten.
Add a scene source and choose a shot to see your sequence here.

960 × 540 WebM with the committed soundtrack when attached, encoded with authored 30 fps timestamps up to 32 MiB. Unsupported audio encoders are refused. Keep this tab visible. Sequence downloads do not add a saved take.
One original PCM16 WAV, mono or stereo at 44.1 or 48 kHz, 1–60 seconds and at most 12 MiB. Audio follows sequence time across clip cuts. Seeking and clip endpoints are silent.
Source seconds round once to the nearest sample frame. Apply all five fields explicitly; unfinished fields are never exported.
No soundtrack. Choose a PCM16 WAV, then explicitly import it. Original bytes are retained; endpoint previews and scrubbing are silent.
Select a sequence clip to choose its source range.

Up to four complete sources, 20 clips and 60 seconds. Undo sequence keeps at most 30 prior snapshots plus current/future; unique retained soundtrack assets also have a 64 MiB budget. Clear sequence Undo deliberately if that budget refuses a new edit.
One set · two performers · up to 20 shots / 60 seconds · your projects stay in this browser.
